title: Carnegie PDSA Redesign
jpTitle: Carnegie Foundation NILSプラットフォーム
summary: Redesigned the Carnegie Foundation's NILS platform PDSA (Plan-Do-Study-Act) workflow. Tested vertical versus horizontal scrolling with users, validated vertical scrolling, then redesigned the Plan and Do phases with step-by-step guidance, progress indicators and collaboration features so the process felt like a guided conversation rather than a form.

angles.product: The interaction question came before the visual one: two competing scroll models were tested with real users first, and only the validated model (vertical scrolling) was carried into the Plan/Do redesign.

mine: Tested two interaction concepts — vertical versus horizontal scrolling — for the multi-step PDSA workflow
Ran user testing that validated vertical scrolling as the most intuitive, least disorienting option
Redesigned the Plan and Do phases with step-by-step guidance, progress indicators and collaboration features
Added document attachment and commenting tools to each phase
team: Lead Product Designer, UI Designer and UX Designer are credited on the page by title; individual contributions are not separated from Takao's

narrative.problem: The PDSA improvement-cycle workflow was inefficient and hard to navigate — users found the interface overwhelming, with too many fields, unclear sequencing, and no sense of progress; the platform meant to support continuous improvement was itself becoming an obstacle.
built: Step-by-step guidance and progress indicators for Plan and Do phases

_notes: The page does not clarify whether the 40%/25% figures are measured post-implementation or projected; recorded with confidence 'stated' since the page does not itself flag them as a projection (unlike CLI Studios, which does).
